issues.segment: moon (visual chip) + caption_ko ('이후 두 번은 창밖 지구를 기준으로…')
issues.problem: The chip '항법 컴퓨터 끈 채 수동 조준' is labelled 'also MCC-7 at 137 h', but that is wrong for MCC-7. Before MCC-7 the LM primary guidance (PGNS) was powered back up and aligned on the Sun and Moon (about 134:15-135:16). The Mission Report says the first move toward firing attitude was made by hand against Earth, but the attitude was then trimmed with primary-guidance steering, and the burn was flown with manual pitch/roll and AGS holding yaw. Only MCC-5 (105:18:28, 14 s at 10% throttle) was flown with the primary guidance powered down, using the terminator cusps on the COAS reticle and the Sun in the telescope. The caption's 'both by hand using Earth' is roughly defensible from the Mission Report, but it hides that the computer was back on for the second burn.
issues.fix_ko: 칩: '항법 컴퓨터 끈 채 수동 조준 (105시간, MCC-5)'로 한정하고 'also MCC-7' 표기는 삭제. 캡션: '이후 105시간에는 항법 컴퓨터를 끈 채 창밖 지구의 낮밤 경계선을 기준으로 손으로 자세를 잡아 궤도를 고쳤고, 재진입 5시간 전 마지막 수정은 다시 켠 항법 장치의 도움을 받았습니다.'
issues.source: Apollo 13 Mission Report MSC-02680 sec. 8.9.1 and 8.9.3 ("With primary guidance available, guidance system steering was manually followed to trim the spacecraft attitudes"); AFJ Day 6 part 4 'The last course correction' 134:15:04-135:16:33 (Sun/Moon P52 alignment), 137:09:13-137:29:46

issues.problem: The fuel cells were in the service module (bay 4), not in the command module Odyssey. The Mission Report describes 'the loss of oxygen and primary power in the service module'.
issues.fix_ko: 1번 탱크의 산소까지 새면서, 오디세이에 전기를 대던 기계선의 연료전지 3개가 모두 멈췄습니다.
issues.source: Mission Report sec. 1.0; Review Board report ch.4 (bay 4 contents)

issues.segment: caption_ko (출처마다 다른 숫자: '추위… 영하였다는 기록은 없습니다')
issues.problem: This is too absolute. No record shows the cabin air below freezing: the CM fell to about 43 F / 6 C, and the LM was typically 54-60 F. But the Mission Report says temperature analysis near the CM potable-water tank and lines shows 'freezing in the lines most likely occurred'. SP-350's caption also says the 'windows frosted'. Read as written, the line contradicts a primary source.
issues.fix_ko: · 추위: 사령선 약 6°C(임무 보고서), 승무원 추정 2~4°C. 지내던 착륙선은 대체로 12~16°C. 선실 공기가 영하였다는 기록은 없지만, 사령선 식수 배관은 얼었던 것으로 추정됩니다(임무 보고서).
issues.source: Mission Report sec. 6.7 ("cabin temperature slowly decreased to approximately 43 F"; "freezing in the lines most likely occurred"; LM "typically between 54 and 60 F"); NASA SP-350 ch.13.4 caption

issues.segment: cold (narration '물은 1인당 하루 약 180mL로 버텼습니다' + gauge visual)
issues.problem: 180 mL/day comes only from Lovell's 1975 recollection: 'six ounces each per day, a fifth of normal intake… and used fruit juices'. The Mission Report is ambiguous ('Not more than 24 ounces of water were consumed by each crewman after the incident'). It also says about 14 lb (~6.3 L) of CM water was moved to the LM 'for drinking and food preparation', and the crew drank juice and ate wet-pack food. Narration with no source suggests 180 mL was their entire fluid intake, which no source supports. The caption attributes it correctly (러벨의 회고), but the narration and the on-screen gauge do not.
issues.fix_ko: 내레이션: '꺼 둔 사령선은 약 3~6도, 마시는 물은 러벨에 따르면 하루 약 180mL로 줄였습니다.' 화면 게이지: '1인당 하루 약 180mL (러벨 회고)'.
issues.source: NASA SP-350 ch.13.3 (Lovell); Mission Report sec. 7.1.5 and 9.2.4

issues.problem: The montage compresses the timeline. The CO2 caution came on at 80:30:53. The indicated peak of 14.9 mmHg (about 85:26) was fixed by switching to the LM's own secondary cartridge, which dropped the reading to 4.6, not by the mailbox. The adapter was read up and built at 90:22-91:10 while the ground read 4.7 mmHg, and it was held out of the loop. It was switched in at about 94:00, when the secondary cartridge reached the 7.6 limit (master alarm at 93:23), and the ground read 0.2 mmHg at 94:33:21. So '수치는 곧 뚝 떨어졌습니다' is true from connection: about 7.6 to 0.2 in about 33 min. The visual must not show the needle falling from about 15, and must not suggest a drop right after the 91:10 assembly.
issues.fix_ko: 내레이션: '지상에서 비닐봉지, 판지, 테이프로 시험한 해법을 불러 줬고, 이 장치를 연결하자 수치는 30여 분 만에 뚝 떨어졌습니다.' 비주얼: 바늘은 7.6 근처에서 바닥으로 떨어지게. 캡션에 한 줄 추가 가능: '최고치 14.9는 착륙선 예비 흡수통으로 바꿔 넘겼고, 우편함 장치는 약 94시간부터 쓰였습니다.'
issues.source: AFJ Day 4 part 2 (080:30:53), part 3 (PAO 85:26 '14.9… dropped to 4.6'), part 4 (091:12:30, 093:23:38-094:00:13), Day 5 part 1 (094:33:21 Kerwin 'reading 0.2'); Mission Report sec. 6.7 (secondary cartridge used 8.5 h)

issues.problem: '착륙선 엔진으로 달 뒤편을 돌아' suggests the engine carried them around the Moon. In fact a 34-s DPS burn at 61:29:43 put them back on a free return, gravity swung them around the far side, and the PC+2 burn at 79:27:39 came after. It is compressed, but it makes the engine sound like the means of circling the Moon.
issues.fix_ko: 착륙선 엔진으로 귀환 궤도를 되찾아 달 뒤편을 돌았고, 창밖 지구를 조준해 손으로 궤도를 고쳤습니다.
issues.source: Mission Report sec. 1.0 and Table 4-III; AFJ Day 3 part 4 (061:29:55)

issues.segment: okjoe / splash / mailbox (attribution and date chips)
issues.problem: These dates are Houston (CST) dates with no time-zone label, while the problem and toocold clips do carry '(휴스턴 시각)'. 'Okay, Joe' (142:46:08) was 17 Apr 11:59 CST, which is 18 Apr 02:59 KST. Splashdown at 18:07 GMT is 18 Apr 03:07 KST. The mailbox remark (80:22:13) was 14 Apr 21:35 CST, which is 15 Apr KST. Korean viewers could read these as Korean dates.
issues.fix_ko: '조 커윈 (휴스턴) · 잭 스와이거트 (오디세이) · 1970.4.17 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)'; 착수 칩 '1970.4.17 (휴스턴 시각) · 남태평양'; 우편함 '밴스 브랜드 · … · 1970.4.14 (휴스턴 시각)'.
issues.source: Mission Report Table 3-1 (range zero 19:13:00 GMT 11 Apr; landing 1807 GMT 17 Apr, sec. 10); GET-to-CST/KST conversion (CST = UTC-6 in Apr 1970; KST = UTC+9)

issues.segment: moon / fix (visuals: 'faceless gloved hands'); where ('white-suit silhouettes')
issues.problem: This is a dramatisation the record contradicts. The crew were not in suits or gloves inside Aquarius or Odyssey. Lovell: 'We considered putting on our spacesuits, but they would have been bulky and too sweaty. Our teflon-coated inflight coveralls…'. For warmth Lovell and Haise wore lunar overshoes and Swigert put on extra underwear. Gloved hands on the controls and on the mailbox build also echo film imagery.
issues.fix_ko: 손은 장갑 없이 작업복 소매의 맨손 실루엣으로. 'where'의 흰 우주복 실루엣도 기내 작업복(코버롤) 실루엣으로 바꾸는 것을 권장.
issues.source: NASA SP-350 ch.13.5 (Lovell) and ch.13.4 caption

issues.problem: Nothing supports 'the venting footage in documentaries is a water dump from another flight'. The searches found nothing, and the AFJ and the 1970 transcript record only Lovell's spoken report. If this note reaches on-screen text or the caption, it is an unsourced claim.
issues.fix_ko: 제작 메모에서 해당 문장 삭제(또는 '미확인' 표시). 화면에는 '일러스트' 표기만 두고 다른 영상에 대한 주장은 넣지 않기.
issues.source: AFJ Day 3 part 2 (056:09:07); 1970 Technical Air-to-Ground Transcript p.~169 (02 08 09 07); web search found no corroboration

issues.segment: caption_ko (crew status: '프레드 헤이즈는 유일한 생존 승무원… (2026년 4월 보도 기준)')

The latest coverage found (Hays Post, 29 Apr 2026; 2025 talks) shows Haise alive, and searches turned up no reports of his death, but that does not confirm his status now. Lovell (d. 7 Aug 2025) and Swigert (d. 27 Dec 1982) are correct.
issues.fix_ko: 게시 직전 최신 뉴스로 재확인 후 '(2026년 11월 기준)'으로 갱신. 문구는 '프레드 헤이즈(1933년생)는 유일한 생존 승무원입니다'.

issues.problem: This is slightly inaccurate. Fourteen minutes after the bang Lovell had already seen the gas cloud and venting out the hatch window (056:09:07), and the crew saw debris early on. What they saw for the first time at 138:04 was the damaged service module itself: the missing bay 4 panel and the stain on the SPS bell.
issues.fix_ko: 기계선을 떼어 내자, 처음으로 부서진 자리가 눈에 들어왔습니다.

issues.segment: okjoe (visual note: '~2.6 s silence… which is the wait')
issues.problem: The 2.6-s gap is only the normal turnaround of an ARIA-relayed exchange, not the blackout wait. The real silence was about 7 min 23 s, from Swigert's 'Thank you' at 142:38:45 to 'Okay, Joe' at 142:46:08, and about 1 min 44 s past the predicted end of blackout. Treating the 2.6 s as 'the wait' overdramatises the clip.
issues.fix_ko: 공백은 그대로 두되 '기다림'으로 연출하지 말고, 긴장감은 앞 장면의 통신 두절 타이머(예상 3분 19초 → +1분 44초)로 처리.

issues.problem: The primary sources describe the bang differently. The 1970 debrief has Lovell's 'dull but definite bang - not much of a vibration'. The Review Board says the crew 'heard a loud bang'. Haise on air (055:56:10) said 'a pretty large bang', and Lovell in SP-350 wrote 'a sharp bang and vibration'. A muffled thud is defensible, but it should not be noted as 'the' record.
issues.fix_ko: 현행 유지 가능. 제작 메모에 '조사위: loud bang / 헤이즈 교신: pretty large bang / 러벨 디브리핑: dull but definite bang'을 함께 적어 두기.
issues.source: AFJ Day 3 part 2 (1970 Technical Debrief quotes; 055:56:10); Review Board report p.4-27; NASA SP-350 ch.13.1

issues.problem: The Board stated this as probable ('the thermostatic switches… were probably welded shut'), not certain. The summary is otherwise accurate.
issues.fix_ko: …28V용 온도 스위치가 65V 전원에 녹아붙은 것으로 추정되며, 히터가 꺼지지 않아 탱크 속 전선 피복이 손상됐고…
issues.source: Review Board report ch.4-5 (findings j-l); NASA SP-350 ch.13.5 quoting the Board

checks.verdict:
Mostly accurate and well sourced. Publish after fixing the MCC-7 chip, the fuel-cell location in the caption and the 'no below-freezing record' wording, and after attributing the water figure, labelling the time zones and re-checking Haise's status.

Checked against primary documents I downloaded: the Mission Report, the Review Board report, the 1970 technical air-to-ground transcript, the AFJ pages and SP-350 ch.13. All seven clips match both the 1970 transcript and the AFJ, word for word, speaker and GET:
- 55:55:35 Lovell, 'Houston, we've had a problem' (AFJ: '[Garble.] Ah, Houston…')
- 56:09:07 Lovell, venting
- 57:24:12 Lousma, LM lifeboat
- 80:22:13 Brand, mailbox
- 132:37:40/59 Swigert, too cold to sleep
- 138:04:46 Lovell, one whole side missing
- 142:46:03 Kerwin and 142:46:08 Swigert; the PAO correction from Lovell to Swigert is confirmed

The file start offsets are consistent with each GET. The Review Board preface quote is verbatim.

These figures also check out:
- About 178,000 nmi from Earth (PAO: 177,861 at 55:47 and 178,643 at 56:12), so about 33만 km is right.
- Fans on at 55:53:20 and tank failure at 55:54:53, so about 1분 반 is right.
- About 87 h from explosion to splashdown, landing in stable 1 about 3.5 nmi from USS Iwo Jima.
- CO2 limit raised from 7.6 to 15 mmHg, indicated peak 14.9, no adverse effects.
- Entry PAD blackout EI+0:19 to EI+3:38 (3 min 19 s); first voice 1 min 44 s after the predicted end; no cause given in the official reports.
- CM about 43 F per the Mission Report, Swigert's 35-40 F estimate, Lovell's 38 F.
- '2 men for 2 days, 3 men nearly 4 days' and '45-hour lifetime' are Lovell's words in SP-350.
- 21:07 CST on 13 Apr is 12:07 KST on 14 Apr.

Myths are handled correctly.

Issues:
- **Factual errors:**
  - The 'computer off' manual-alignment chip also claims MCC-7, but the LM primary guidance was powered back up and Sun/Moon-aligned before that burn.
  - The caption puts the fuel cells in Odyssey (the CM); they were in the service module.
- **Overstatements:**
  - 'No record of below-freezing' ignores the Mission Report's finding that the CM water lines most likely froze.
  - The 180 mL/day water figure is only Lovell's recollection, and the narration doesn't attribute it.
  - The CO2 montage hides that the 14.9 peak was solved by the LM spare cartridge; the mailbox went into use at about 94:00 and the reading fell to 0.2 by 94:33.
- **Smaller points:**
  - Several 17 Apr dates are Houston dates (18 Apr in Korea) with no label.
  - The gloved hands and white suits contradict Lovell's account; the crew wore coveralls.
  - The 'documentary venting footage is a water dump' note has no source.
  - Haise's status needs re-checking, since the caption's cut-off is April 2026 and today is November 2026.

checks.verdict:
Six of the seven audio clips pass, with only small trims needed; one (venting) needs a real fix before rendering. For every clip I re-transcribed the exact range and a ±4 s window with faster-whisper medium (word timestamps) and checked the start and end points with 40-50 ms energy envelopes and Quindar-tone (2525/2475 Hz) detection. Speakers were checked against TEC (1970), AIRT and AFJ, with median pitch as extra evidence: Lovell 132-141 Hz on tape 414, Swigert 155-175 Hz.

- **problem**: words and speaker (Lovell) are correct and the range has no tone. The 'Uh/Ah' before 'Houston' is a garble that can't be resolved; cutting at 30.70 is cleaner.
- **venting**: must fix. The clip starts inside a loud CAPCOM key tone and cuts off Lovell's false start 'We are -'. The AFJ MP3 cross-correlation (r=0.98) confirms that false start is Lovell's voice. Switch to Apollo-13-Problem.ogg 395.95-399.70 s, or start at 24.42 with notch filters. Update words_en to 'We are - we are venting...'.
- **lifeboat**: correct and clean. Adjust subtitle timing so 'and' falls before the pause; the intro beep is full level.
- **mailbox**: verbatim. Start 0.08 s earlier (23.22).
- **toocold**: verbatim, and the speaker is confirmed as Swigert. Extend the end to 30.95 or fade it out.
- **missing**: verbatim and clean as is.
- **okjoe**: Kerwin's line is clean. ASR can't confirm 'Joe' on the ARIA relay, but TEC, AIRT, the PAO comment and Kerwin's 'We read you, Jack' all support 'Okay, Joe' from Swigert.

Other quotes:
- The closing Review Board quote matches the report's preface verbatim.
- 'Farewell, Aquarius, and we thank you' is Kerwin at 141:30:05.
- The water figure is correct: SP-350 says six ounces per person per day, about 177 mL.
- Event times match the Mission Report: SM separation 138:01:48, entry interface 142:40:46, splashdown 142:54:41.

No film lines are used as real quotes, and none of the Korean subtitles are wrong; the subtitle suggestions above are optional wording tweaks.

The script is usable and the core lines work: '두 사람이 이틀… 세 사람이 나흘', the 네모/동그라미 image, and '세 사람 모두, 살아 돌아왔습니다.' Five things need fixing before TTS. (1) '2번 탱크' is read as '이 번 탱크', which sounds like 이번 ('this time'). (2) The TTS strings for where, tank, cold, blackout and splash have more words than the say strings, so build.py's 'say/tts word count mismatch' check will stop the build in blocks mode. (3) Lay viewers are never told what 사령선, 기계선 or 오디세이 are. (4) The moon line says the lander's engine took them around the Moon; it was a free-return path, and the engine only made corrections. Moon landing being called off is also never said. (5) The cold line packs in too many numbers ('삼 도에서 육 도', '일 인당', '백팔십 밀리리터'). The hook is stronger with the recognisable name 아폴로 13호 in it. Pacing: the previous reels used the same Hyunsu voice at +18% and measured 5.6–5.8 syllables per second, plus about 0.5 s per scene. On that basis the script runs about 108–110 s, not the 105 s the est_seconds add up to. The rewrites below keep the narration at about the same length (384 → 389 syllables) while making it clearer, so reaching ~100 s also needs the clip trims and the ranked cuts in the pacing item.

issues.source: caption figures; Lovell 6 oz/day

issues.problem: This is the first time '기계선' is heard, and it is never explained. Viewers won't connect it to the part where the tank burst.
issues.fix_ko:
탱크가 터진 기계선을 떼어 내자, 처음으로 폭발 흔적이 보였습니다.
(+5 syllables. Shorter alternative: keep the original line and label the cylinder on screen '기계선 (산소 탱크가 있던 곳)'.)
issues.source: editorial clarity

issues.problem: '재진입 통신 두절,' is a stack of nouns. TTS reads it flatly and lay viewers may not follow it. Saying first that the radio cut out as expected sets up the 'longer than expected' tension. TTS word count also needs fixing ('일 분' → '일분').
issues.fix_ko:
say: 대기권에 들어서자 무전이 끊겼고, 예상보다 1분 넘게 신호가 없었습니다.
TTS: 대기권에 들어서자 무전이 끊겼고, 예상보다 일분 넘게 신호가 없었습니다.
(9 words each, 30 syllables, about 5.3 s.)
issues.source: editorial clarity; build.py assert

issues.problem: In the narration '오디세이' is only ever a visual label, so here the name arrives with no explanation. After 'Okay, Joe' the subject is obvious anyway. Dropping it saves about 0.9 s.
issues.fix_ko:
say: 폭발 약 87시간 만에, 남태평양에 내려앉았습니다.
TTS: 폭발 약 팔십칠시간 만에, 남태평양에 내려앉았습니다.
issues.source: pacing calc

issues.problem: '오디세이' in the subtitle is unknown to viewers, and the clip comes right before the payoff.
issues.fix_ko:
오디세이(사령선), 휴스턴 대기 중. / 오버. / 오케이, 조.
(Same style as the '(산소 압력이)' note in the lifeboat subtitle.)
issues.source: editorial clarity

issues.problem: The comma in '조사위원회는,' makes an odd TTS pause after the topic marker. The line also ends on a flat '적었습니다' when the reveal (crew and ground team) should come last, which is the cadence of the Lemons closer.
issues.fix_ko:
조사위원회의 평가, 재앙을 막은 건 승무원, 그리고 지상 관제팀이었습니다.
(29 syllables, about 5.1 s. The verbatim English quote stays on the card.)
issues.source: Report of Apollo 13 Review Board preface (quote in visual)

issues.problem: Here 'As it turns out' means 'as it happens'. '알고 보니' means a discovery in the past and clashes with the future tense in '생길 겁니다'. Starting the clip at 'this contraption' fixes this and saves about 0.7 s. Whisper word timings put 'this' at 24.00 and 'out' ending at 24.00.
issues.fix_ko: Clip start 23.30 → 23.98. Subtitles: '이 장치는 우편함처럼 생길 겁니다,' (24.00–26.42) / '다 조립하고 나면요.' (26.42–28.45). If you keep the full clip, change the first chunk to '결국 이 장치는'.
issues.source: faster-whisper small word timestamps on a13_05_mailbox (this@24.00, contraption@24.26)

issues.problem: '쓰는 걸 생각하고 있습니다' is a literal translation. '다들 같은 문제예요' sounds like translationese.
issues.fix_ko:
lifeboat: '이제 착륙선을 구명정으로' / '쓰는 방안을 검토하고 있습니다.'
toocold: '다들 마찬가지예요.' / '너무 추워서 잠을 못 자요.'
issues.source: editorial

issues.problem: Using the previous reels' measured rate (5.6–5.8 syllables/s for Hyunsu at +18%, plus about 0.5 s per scene and a 1.8 s end pad), the script as written runs about 108–110 s; the est_seconds sum of 105.2 is too low. The rewrites above keep the narration at about the same length. Trimming the mailbox clip start (−0.7 s) and starting the lifeboat clip at 10.42 to drop the Quindar beep (−0.4 s) bring it to about 107 s. Hitting ~100 s needs some of the ranked cuts below.
issues.fix_ko:
Ranked cuts:
① lifeboat clip: keep only 'we're starting to think about the LM lifeboat' (start about 12.8 s, check by ear) → −2.4 s. 'It's slowly going to zero' is a strong line, so only cut it if you have to.
② moon: '달 착륙은 포기하고, 달 뒤편을 돌아 지구로 향했습니다.' → −2 s. The manual aiming moves to the on-screen chip '창밖 지구로 수동 조준'.
③ close: '재앙을 막은 건, 승무원과 지상 관제팀이었습니다.' with the source on the quote card → −1.8 s.
④ smsep: keep the original line and add an on-screen label → −0.9 s.
With ①+②+③ the reel runs about 101–103 s.
issues.source: projects/lemons & okene build/timeline.json (measured syll/s); pacing calc

issues.problem: '사령선 오디세이의 연료전지가 모두 멈췄습니다' is wrong: the fuel cells were in the service module (기계선), not the command module.
issues.fix_ko: 1번 탱크의 산소까지 새면서 기계선의 연료전지 3개가 모두 멈췄고, 사령선 '오디세이'에는 재진입용 배터리만 남았습니다.
issues.source: Report of Apollo 13 Review Board (SM EPS)

segments.narration_ko: 달로 가던 아폴로 13호에서, '쾅' 소리가 났습니다.
segments.visual: Black starfield. A tiny, flat code-drawn docked stack (cone CM + cylinder SM + spidery LM; no NASA logo, flag or mission patch) drifts toward a small crescent Moon. On '쾅': a white flash on one side of the cylindrical SM, a panel flies off, glittering spray, a 1-frame shake. SFX: a short, muffled low thud, not a Hollywood fireball. The sources describe the bang differently (Review Board: 'loud bang'; Haise on air at 55:56:10: 'a pretty large bang'; Lovell's 1970 debrief: 'a dull but definite bang - not much of a vibration'), so none of them is 'the' sound. Title overlay: 우주에서 터진 산소탱크 / 2인용 구명정에 3명. TTS: 달로 가던 아폴로 십삼호에서, 쾅 소리가 났습니다.

segments.attribution: 짐 러벨 선장 · 1970.4.13 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: Radio-waveform card over a dim cabin silhouette. Large English line: "Houston, we've had a problem." plus a small note: ※ 영화(1995) 속 'we have a problem'은 잘못 알려진 표현. Subtitle timing: 30.76-32.05 as one line (speech 30.78-31.84; 'Houston,' ends about 31.11). GET 55:55:35, about 42 s after the tank failure. Clean air-to-ground audio with no Quindar; silence from 31.85. The start moved from 30.10 to 30.70 (quiet gap 30.64-30.75, about -44 dBFS) to drop a short garbled sound before 'Houston' that the sources render differently (AFJ '[Garble.] Ah', AIRT 'Uh', 1970 TEC nothing). 'Houston, we've had a problem.' is word for word in TEC 02 07 55 35, AIRT and AFJ, and the voice matches Lovell's other tape-414 lines. Swigert's first call about 15 s earlier is disputed in wording and speaker, so it is not used.

segments.narration_ko: 1970년 4월, 지구에서 약 33만 km.
segments.visual: Simple map: Earth at bottom-left, Moon at top-right, a dotted outbound path, and the spacecraft marker most of the way to the Moon, labelled '지구에서 약 33만 km' (PAO readouts: about 178,000 nautical miles). Chips: '1970.04' and plain-type 'APOLLO 13' (no patch or logo). Three faceless silhouettes in plain inflight coveralls (not white spacesuits: the crew wore coveralls inside the cabins) labelled 짐 러벨 (선장) · 잭 스와이거트 · 프레드 헤이즈. TTS: 천구백칠십년 사월, 지구에서 약 삼십삼만 킬로미터.

segments.narration_ko: 산소 탱크를 휘저은 지 1분 반 만에, 그중 하나가 터졌습니다.
segments.visual: Cutaway of the service module: two round tanks in one bay, labelled 산소 탱크 1 · 2 (keep the labels so viewers see it was tank 2). Both tanks' internal fan icons start spinning (a routine 'cryo stir' Houston had asked for; tank 2 fans on at 55:53:20) while a small timer counts 0:00 to 1:33 (tank 2 failure 55:54:53). A spark runs along the wiring inside tank 2, the tank ruptures and the outer bay panel blows off. TTS: 산소 탱크를 휘저은 지 일분 반 만에, 그중 하나가 터졌습니다.

clip.words_en: We are - we are venting something out into the - into space.
clip.speaker: Jim Lovell (CDR, Apollo 13)

subtitle_ko.en: We are - we are venting something

segments.attribution: 짐 러벨 선장 · 폭발 약 14분 뒤 · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: A faceless silhouette at the small hatch window. Outside, a glittering white gas cloud streams away. This is illustration only: the crew took no photos of the venting, and the AFJ editors note that documentaries often illustrate this exchange with 16-mm footage of a water dump from an earlier flight. New audio file: a 14 s excerpt (local 0.0 s = 390.0 s) of Apollo-13-Problem.ogg in the same Internet Archive item 'Apollo13Audio' (NASA JSC digitization, Public Domain Mark), 48 kHz mono. This cut has no Quindar tone (noise floor about -38 dBFS); speech runs 6.04-9.56 and includes Lovell's false start 'We are -'. Subtitle timing: 6.00-7.60 / 7.60-9.60. GET 56:09:07; AFJ has 'We are - We are venting something out into the - into space.' (AIRT and TEC leave out the stutter). Fallback if the new file is not used: a13_02 WAV 24.42-28.15 with notch filters at 2525/2475/5050/4950 Hz (Q about 12) over 24.30-25.35 only. Never start at 24.52 (inside a full-level CAPCOM key tone) or at 25.00 (mid-word).

segments.narration_ko: 새어 나간 건 숨 쉴 산소이자, 전기와 물의 원료였습니다.
segments.visual: Instrument panel close-up: the 'O2 TANK 1' needle slides toward 0, and three fuel-cell icons in the service module (연료전지 1 · 2 · 3) go dark one by one. Cells 1 and 3 lost oxygen within seconds of the failure; cell 2 ran on tank 1 for about 2 more hours. Small 숨, 전기 and 물 icons fade, and the cabin lights dim.

clip.words_en: It's slowly going to zero, and we're starting to think about the LM lifeboat.
clip.speaker: Jack Lousma (CAPCOM, Mission Control Houston)

segments.attribution: 잭 루스마 · 휴스턴 교신 담당 (CAPCOM) · 폭발 약 1시간 반 뒤 · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: Mission Control as faceless silhouettes at rows of consoles (no logos), with radio waves going out to the spacecraft. The start moved to 10.42 (noise floor about -42 dBFS) to drop the full-level Quindar intro beep at 10.10-10.38. Speech runs 10.50-15.38, and the outro beep at 15.70 is excluded. Subtitle timing: 10.50-11.20 / 11.20-12.40 / 13.10-14.20 / 14.20-15.40 ('and' is spoken before the pause and ends about 12.38). Context: at GET 57:24:09 Swigert had just asked whether the O2 tank 1 pressure was still going down. This line is GET 57:24:12, verbatim 'the LM lifeboat' in TEC, AIRT and AFJ (ASR mishears 'LEM lifeboats').

segments.narration_ko: 두 사람이 이틀 쓰도록 만든 달 착륙선에서, 세 사람이 나흘 가까이 버텨야 했습니다.
segments.visual: Side view of the docked stack: the CM, labelled 오디세이 (사령선), goes dark and the LM, labelled 아쿠아리우스 (달 착륙선), lights up. Inside the LM, two standing outlines carry the label '설계: 2명 · 약 45시간'; a third silhouette in coveralls squeezes in and a counter reads '실제: 3명 · 약 84시간' (power-up about 57:42 to undocking 141:30). Lovell, SP-350: 'designed to support two men for two days... three men nearly four days' and 'a 45-hour lifetime'.

segments.narration_ko: 달 착륙은 포기하고, 달 뒤편을 돌아 지구로 향했습니다.
segments.visual: Trajectory: a figure-8 path around the Moon's far side. The Fra Mauro landing marker greys out. Small LM descent-engine flashes mark the two burns: GET 61:30, back onto a free return, and GET 79:28, PC+2 after the far side, which sped up the return and moved the landing to the Pacific. The Moon's gravity, not the engine, swings the path around. Then a window view: an Earth crescent with its day/night line (terminator) laid on a crosshair reticle, the Sun in a small scope, and faceless bare hands in coverall sleeves (no gloves, no suits) on the hand controllers. Chip: '항법 컴퓨터 끈 채, 창밖 지구로 수동 조준 (발사 105시간째)'. That was MCC-5 at 105:18 (14 s at 10% throttle). Do not label the final correction (MCC-7, about 137:40) as computer-off: the LM primary guidance was powered back up and aligned on the Sun and Moon before it.

segments.narration_ko: 이산화탄소는 쌓여 가는데, 사령선 필터는 네모, 착륙선 구멍은 동그라미였습니다.
segments.visual: A CO2 gauge needle creeps past the 7.6 mmHg caution mark (label 경고) and a caution light blinks (first at GET 80:30:53). No 'lethal' labels, and do not show the needle near 15. Then a square canister (사령선 필터, 네모) bumps uselessly against a round socket (착륙선 구멍, 동그라미): a square peg and a round hole.

clip.words_en: As it turns out, this contraption will look like a mailbox, when you get it all put together.
clip.speaker: Vance Brand (CAPCOM, Mission Control Houston)

subtitle_ko.en: As it turns out, this contraption
when you get it all put together.

segments.attribution: 밴스 브랜드 · 휴스턴 교신 담당 (CAPCOM) · 1970.4.14 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: A blueprint-style sketch on a Houston desk (the ground side, not the spacecraft) of a box with a plastic 'roof' that looks like a mailbox, drawing itself line by line. There is light hiss (noise floor about -31 dB). The start moved to 23.22 (hiss about -28 dBFS) so the clip fade-in does not soften 'As' (onset 23.34). Subtitle timing: 23.35-25.04 / 25.04-26.42 / 26.42-28.45. GET 80:22:13 (21:35 CST; 15 Apr in Korea), verbatim in AIRT and TEC. Brand's Quindar beep at 28.75 is excluded.

segments.narration_ko: 비닐봉지, 판지, 테이프로 만들어 연결하자, 이산화탄소가 뚝 떨어졌습니다.
segments.visual: Split screen. Left: faceless ground engineers (label '지상에서 설계·시험') assemble a mock-up on a table. Right: in the LM, bare hands in coverall sleeves (no gloves) wrap gray tape sticky side out around the square canister, then add a plastic bag, a bent cardboard card and a red suit hose, and the 'mailbox' is finished. Then the hose is connected, airflow arrows run through it, and the CO2 needle falls from about the 7.6 caution mark toward the bottom, with a small chip '0.2 mmHg (GET 94:33, 지상 판독)'. Labels: 비닐봉지 · 판지 · 덕트 테이프 · 우주복 호스. Do not show the needle falling from about 15: the 14.9 peak (about 85 h) was handled by switching to the LM's own spare cartridge. Facts: MSC Crew Systems Division engineers designed and tested it. Kerwin listed the equipment at 90:09 and read the steps from 90:22:50. The first unit was reported done at 91:10:26 and held out of the loop while the ground read 4.7. It was switched in from about 93:27 when the LM cartridge reached its limit, and the ground read 0.2 at 94:33:21.

segments.narration_ko: 꺼 둔 사령선은 냉장고처럼 차가웠고, 물도 아껴 마셔야 했습니다.
segments.visual: Dark CM interior with a thermometer showing 약 3~6°C, and windows and walls beaded with condensation. A chip quotes the crew's own nickname for the CM: 'the refrigerator' (Swigert, GET 127:34:33: 'we used to call the Command Module the bedroom and it's now the refrigerator'). A paper-cup icon is labelled '물: 1인당 하루 약 180mL (러벨 회고)'. Blue-grey palette. No snow or icicles: no record puts the cabin air below freezing.

clip.words_en: All of us have that same problem. It's just too cold to sleep.
clip.speaker: Jack Swigert (CMP, Apollo 13)

subtitle_ko.en: All of us have that same problem.
It's just too cold to sleep.

segments.attribution: 잭 스와이거트 · 1970.4.17 새벽 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: Three faceless silhouettes in coveralls huddled in the small LM cabin under a frost-blue tint, one curled on the engine cover. The end moved from 30.65 to 30.95 so the cut lands after the downlink noise tail (30.45-30.92 about -36 dBFS; floor -42 from 30.96). Subtitle timing: 26.40-28.90 / 28.95-30.60. GET 132:37:59, verbatim in AIRT and TEC (CMP). CAPCOM Lousma had asked 'How much sleep did you get, Jack?'. Clean audio.

segments.narration_ko: 기계선을 떼어 내자, 처음으로 부서진 자리가 보였습니다.
segments.visual: Window view: the cylindrical SM, labelled '기계선 (산소 탱크가 있던 곳)', drifts away and slowly turns, revealing one side panel gone, with torn insulation and debris and a brown streak near the engine bell. Chip: '재진입 약 4시간 반 전'. SM jettison was at GET 138:01:48. The crew had seen venting gas and debris right after the bang; this was their first look at the damaged module itself.

clip.words_en: And there's one whole side of that spacecraft missing.
clip.speaker: Jim Lovell (CDR, Apollo 13)

segments.attribution: 짐 러벨 선장 · 1970.4.17 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: Hold on the damaged SM shrinking into black. Subtitle timing: 20.25-21.80 / 21.80-23.05. GET 138:04:46, verbatim in TEC, AIRT, AFJ and SP-350. This tape track also carries PAO commentary, but this window is clean: speech 20.25-22.95, floor -40 dBFS from 23.00, and Kerwin's 'Is that right?' starts at 25.13.

segments.narration_ko: 재진입 중 무전이 끊겼고, 예상보다 1분 넘게 조용했습니다.
segments.visual: First the LM Aquarius is released (small chip: '착륙선 분리 · 재진입 약 1시간 전'). Optionally show CAPCOM Kerwin's 'Farewell, Aquarius, and we thank you.' (GET 141:30:05) as on-screen text credited to Houston, not the crew. Then the cone capsule glows orange in plasma and a radio-wave icon is crossed out. A timer labelled '예상 통신 두절 약 3분 19초' runs out, then keeps counting in red to '+1:44' (first crew voice). On the ground, silent silhouettes wait at the consoles. Do not claim a cause such as the shallow entry angle; the official reports give none. TTS: 재진입 중 무전이 끊겼고, 예상보다 일분 넘게 조용했습니다.

clip.words_en: Odyssey, Houston standing by. Over. / Okay, Joe.
clip.speaker: Joe Kerwin (CAPCOM, Houston) / Jack Swigert (CMP, in Odyssey)

segments.attribution: 조 커윈 (휴스턴) · 잭 스와이거트 (오디세이) · 1970.4.17 (휴스턴 시각) · NASA 교신 음성 (퍼블릭 도메인)
segments.visual: Waveform card: Kerwin's call, a short crackling gap, then Swigert's reply. The ~2.6 s gap (12.45-15.05) is the normal turnaround of a call relayed through the ARIA 4 aircraft, not the blackout wait. Keep it but don't dramatise it; the previous scene's timer carries the tension. The end moved from 16.35 to 16.45 (residual noise ends 16.42). Subtitle timing: 10.10-11.85 / 11.85-12.45 / 15.05-16.40. GET 142:46:03 and 142:46:08 (11:59 CST; 18 Apr 02:59 in Korea). ASR can't confirm 'Joe' on the relay audio, but TEC (05 22 46 08 CMP 'Okay, Joe.'), AIRT, the PAO comment and Kerwin's reply 'Okay. We read you, Jack.' all support it. The NASA PAO first credited 'Okay, Joe' to Lovell, then corrected it to Swigert.

segments.narration_ko: 폭발 약 87시간 만에, 남태평양에 내려앉았습니다.
segments.visual: Three orange-and-white parachutes over a blue ocean. The capsule, labelled 오디세이, touches down upright, with a recovery-ship silhouette on the horizon (USS Iwo Jima, about 6.5 km away). Chip: '1970.4.17 (휴스턴 시각) · 남태평양'. Splashdown was at GET 142:54:41 (12:07 CST; 18 Apr 03:07 in Korea), 86 h 59 min after the tank failure. TTS: 폭발 약 팔십칠시간 만에, 남태평양에 내려앉았습니다.

segments.narration_ko: 세 사람 모두, 살아 돌아왔습니다.
segments.visual: Three faceless silhouettes in a life raft beside the capsule as a helicopter hovers above. Text: '3명 전원 생환'. The music resolves.

segments.narration_ko: 재앙을 막은 건, 승무원과 지상 관제팀이었습니다.
segments.visual: Quote card on a dark background with a faint Earth and Moon: "...a near disaster, averted only by outstanding performance on the part of the crew and the ground control team which supported them." - Report of Apollo 13 Review Board, June 1970 (verbatim from the report's preface). A small Korean translation sits under it: (번역) 승무원과 그들을 지원한 지상 관제팀의 뛰어난 활약으로 겨우 피한, 재앙에 가까운 사고. End card.

final.caption_ko:
[실화] 지구에서 약 33만 km, 산소 탱크가 터진 아폴로 13호
※ 실제 NASA 교신 음성(1970)이 포함되어 있습니다.

1970년 4월 13일 밤 9시 8분경(휴스턴 시각, 한국 시각 14일 낮 12시 8분경), 달로 가던 아폴로 13호의 기계선에서 2번 산소 탱크가 터졌습니다. 탱크 속 산소를 휘젓는 팬을 켠 지 약 1분 반 뒤였습니다. 승무원은 선장 짐 러벨, 사령선 조종사 잭 스와이거트, 착륙선 조종사 프레드 헤이즈.

폭발 충격과 1번 탱크의 누출로, 사령선 '오디세이'에 전기와 물을 대던 기계선의 연료전지 3개가 모두 멈췄습니다. 세 사람은 재진입용 배터리를 아끼려 사령선을 끄고, 두 사람이 약 45시간 쓰도록 만든 착륙선 '아쿠아리우스'에서 약 84시간을 버텼습니다.

착륙선의 이산화탄소 흡수통은 귀환까지 모자랐고, 사령선 흡수통은 모양이 맞지 않았습니다. 휴스턴 엔지니어들이 비닐봉지·판지·덕트 테이프·우주복 호스로 만든 어댑터('우편함')를 지상에서 먼저 시험했고, 교신으로 단계별로 불러 줬습니다.

이미 자동 귀환 궤도를 벗어나 있었기에, 착륙선 엔진으로 귀환 궤도를 되찾고 달 뒤편을 돈 뒤 다시 점화해 귀환을 앞당겼습니다. 발사 105시간째에는 항법 컴퓨터를 끈 채 창밖 지구의 낮밤 경계선을 기준으로 손으로 자세를 잡아 궤도를 고쳤고, 재진입 약 5시간 전 마지막 수정은 다시 켠 항법 장치의 도움을 받았습니다. 4월 17일(휴스턴 시각) 남태평양에 착수해, 폭발 약 87시간 만에 세 사람 모두 살아 돌아왔습니다.

출처마다 다른 숫자와 기록
· 폭발 지점: NASA 발표 약 17만 8천 해리(약 33만 km). '20만 마일'은 어림수입니다.
· 추위: 사령선 약 6°C(임무 보고서), 승무원 추정 2~4°C. 지내던 착륙선은 대체로 12~16°C. 선실 공기가 영하였다는 기록은 없지만, 사령선 식수 배관은 얼었던 것으로 추정됩니다(임무 보고서).
· 물: 하루 약 180mL는 러벨의 회고이고, 임무 보고서는 '사고 후 1인당 24온스(약 710mL) 이하'로 적었습니다. 주스는 따로 마셨습니다.
· 이산화탄소: 경고 기준 7.6 mmHg를 의료진이 15로 올렸고, 최고치 14.9는 착륙선 예비 흡수통으로 바꿔 넘겼습니다. '우편함'은 발사 약 94시간째부터 쓰였고, 건강 이상은 없었습니다(임무 보고서).
· 통신 두절: 예측 약 3분 19초, 첫 음성은 예측보다 약 1분 44초 늦었습니다. 늦어진 이유는 공식 보고서에 없습니다.
· 첫 호출 "Okay, Houston… we've had a problem here"는 기록마다 화자와 문구가 조금 다릅니다. 영상 속 음성은 이견이 없는 러벨의 두 번째 호출입니다.
· "Houston, we have a problem"과 "Failure is not an option"은 1995년 영화 대사로, 실제 교신에는 없습니다.
· 가스가 새는 장면은 사진·영상이 남아 있지 않습니다(Apollo Flight Journal).

원인(NASA 조사위원회, 1970): 발사 전 지상 작업에서 28V용 온도 스위치가 65V 전원에 녹아붙은 것으로 추정되며, 히터가 꺼지지 않아 탱크 속 전선 피복이 손상됐고, 비행 중 합선으로 불이 나 탱크가 터졌습니다.

짐 러벨은 2025년, 잭 스와이거트는 1982년 세상을 떠났습니다. 프레드 헤이즈(1933년생)는 유일한 생존 승무원입니다(2026년 11월 기준).
